newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Air Jamaica losses mount to US$75 million.
newsitem.headline: Air Jamaica losses mount to US$75 million.

text.p: Air Jamaica chairman Gordon "Butch" Stewart said Friday the carrier has racked up losses of US$75 million in the past 21 months and the Jamaican government is expected to increase its equity to compensate.

Two months ago, airline officials said the total losses stood at US$30 million and they expected the airline to break even in 1997. Air Jamaica's troubles began when the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration gave Jamaica's civil aviation department a category II rating, effectively grounding the airline's fleet of brand-new Airbus A310s.

Stewart said the Jamaican government, which presently owns 25 percent of Air Jamaica, was expected to inject another US$20 million to $25 million in return for preference shares, in order to compensate for the losses.
He said FAA inspectors were expected in Kingston next month, at which time Jamaica's category I rating should be restored.

Air Jamaica will begin flying new routes between North America and Antigua, Barbados, St. Lucia and Trinidad early next year. Officials said the new routes are necessary if Air Jamaica is to achieve its target of 24 percent passenger growth a year over the next three years.
